programme.title: The Secret Life of the Sun
programme.desc: Ninety million miles away from us is the power that shapes our world - the Sun. Using the latest satellite images, and the expertise of Britain's leading solar scientists, Kate Humble and Helen Czerski reveal the inner workings of our very own star, and the influence its mysterious cycles of activity have on our planet.

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: As transatlantic liners brought America's super-rich to the region, art and celebrity became integrally intertwined as cultural gurus and multi-millionaires all partied on the beach. In an era of sunshine and bathing, of cinema and fast cars, of the Ballet Russes and Monte Carlo casinos, Richard E Grant discovers the extraordinary output of what became briefly the world's creative hub.

programme.title: The Jet Stream and Us
programme.desc: A look at how human understanding of the jet stream, a ribbon of fast moving air high in the atmosphere, has grown. It has been responsible for bewildering effects on bomber pilots during WWII, the 1987 hurricane and devastating floods.

programme.title: Dusty Springfield at the BBC
programme.desc: A second chance to explore the BBC's archives with one of British music's biggest and best-loved stars, Dusty Springfield. The great soul diva and her haunting voice are captured once again in a selection of BBC performances from over the years.

programme.title: Dusty Springfield at the BBC
programme.desc: A selection of Dusty Springfield's performances at the BBC from 1961 to 1995. Dusty was one of Britain's great pop divas, guaranteed to give a big melody in songs soaring with drama and yearning.

programme.title: Sad Songs at the BBC

programme.title: Attenborough's Passion Projects
programme.desc: First transmitted in 1989, 'Lost Worlds, Vanished Lives' showcases the world's major fossil sites. In a number of specially shot interviews, Attenborough introduces extracts from the series, where he reveals ancient sea creatures, sabre-toothed predators and immense dinosaurs. Ground-breaking for its time and still as relevant now, David explores how fossils fire the imagination and teach us about the lives of long extinct animals, and also the world they lived in.

programme.title: Darcey Bussell on The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: Renowned ballet dancer Dame Darcey Bussell introduces a gem from the BBC's dance archives, 'The Magic of Dance'. Darcey describes her favourite moments of the series, including a tap masterclass with the ever-cool Sammy Davis Jr.

programme.title: The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: Margot Fonteyn discusses how the role of the male in dance evolved throughout the 20th century. Her story is illustrated by some of the world's greatest dancers performing some of the era's most enduring dances.

programme.title: Sammy Davis Jr at the BBC
programme.desc: He was known as Mr Entertainment, and it's clear why that was the case from this collection of some of Sammy Davis Jr's finest moments on British television - showing off his unbeatable talents as singer and raconteur and opening up about his life in several fascinating conversations.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Bettany Hughes travels to China on the trail of Confucius, a great sage of Chinese history whose ideas have fundamentally shaped the country of his birth for around 2,500 years.
